body.p: Sparrows. Once there lived a sparrow. Its nest was on some bank of a river. It flies to warmer climes, then returns and builds its nest in the same place near the pine forest on the bank. It flies there. One day he looks: a little mouse. You can hear the sparrow saying there: âOh, how beautiful you are! Marry my son!" He startet looking. Then the father of the mouse says: âWhy not, she hasnât been married yet. Take the bride. After that, your son must live with us for one year.â During the summer, everyone lived together while it was warm. With the onset of cold weather, sparrows flew to warmer climes. Sparrow says: "Let our comrade stay here, he will live for a year." The mouse says: âLet our son-in-law spend the winter with us, he will stay for a year.â The sparrow family said, "Of course it will." All the sparrows flew away to warmer climes. The mouse son-in-law remained there in the hole. Here comes the cold. And the sparrows all live at the door to the hole. The mice far in the hole had nuts, which were collected in the summer, there were mushrooms. The Mouse himself and his children lived at the end of the hole. The little sparrow had a bed near the door, and he had to live there, poor thing, and he froze there. Every day the Mouse came up to him and checked whether he was breathing or not breathing. Everything checks and checks, and suddenly the breath disappeared. The mouse said: âMy poor son-in-law, his breath hitched. This evening we eat son-in-law's meat. Sparrow meat is what we eat. What can I say, he didnât even give anything to the children, he swallowed the meat of his son-in-law. So this Mouse swallowed his son-in-law in an instant, without even chewing. Now the Mouse himself lived near the door. Now the time of spring has come, sparrows have flown from the warm edges. They ask: âMouse, where does your son-in-law live? Where did you send him?" The mouse turned away and said nothing. The whole flock of sparrows went to him, stood up from both sides. âTell, where is your son-in-law?â He does not look them in the face, he says: "He was freezing, so I ate him." Then the sparrows all jumped on him, pressing his stomach to the ground. The Mouse's belly burst. And from there the sparrow flew out and said: âAty-chiv, aty-chiv, aty-chiv.â And flew. After all, the inside of the Mouse's stomach was warm. During the winter, our sparrow lived inside the stomach of the Mouse. The mouse wanted to wipe the sparrow off the face of the earth, but as a result he himself lost.
